title: Overage billed after throttling: duplicate token accounting across gateway retries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer reported unexpected February invoice spike where throttled requests appear billed multiple times. Initial support escalation from Acme Health indicated ~35% higher token charge on streaming generations where SDK/agent reported 429s and client-side retries were observed. This ticket tracks the investigation, fixes, credits, and postmortem for duplicate usage counting triggered by the gateway throttling behavior.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a heavy concurrent streaming workload (50 concurrent streams) using SDK v1.12 configured with client-side exponential backoff and 3 retries.
2) Configure project with soft quota of 100k tokens/min to trigger gateway throttling in integration environment.
3) Observe gateway returning 429 and SDK performing a retry without preserving the original X-Request-Id header.
4) Inspect /billing/usage-accumulator to see multiple entries for effectively the same logical request_id and token_count recorded across retries.
5) Run billing reconciliation for the day and note duplicate token counts are not deduped when request_id missing or altered.
Expected result: throttled/retied requests deduplicated; only successfully persisted tokens billed once.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-28: Support ticket opened by CS (Case #CH-2298) after Acme Health disputed Feb invoice. Customer provided sample request_ids with timestamps and SDK logs showing 429s followed by immediate retry.

2026-03-01: Pulled raw events from ingress logs for customer org-id: org-acme-001. Observed ~12k request entries where request_id changed between initial call and retry (missing X-Request-Id on retry), causing accumulator to treat them as separate events.

2026-03-02: Billing batch job (daily-accumulate-v2) groups records by request_id to dedupe. When request_id absent, dedupe key falls back to client_timestamp+client_ip which can differ across retries on edge proxies.

2026-03-03: Reproduced locally with SDK v1.12 and gateway env staging: SDK retry path does not copy X-Request-Id header when receiving 429 from gateway, resulting in new UUID on retry path at the proxy layer.

2026-03-04: Kernel team reviewed ingestion pipeline and confirmed no dedupe performed on combination of original_event_id and retry_marker because retry_marker is only populated for 5xx server errors, not for 429 throttles.

2026-03-05: Drafted two potential mitigation approaches: (A) make gateway set Retry-Origin header so retries carry original idempotency key; (B) change billing dedupe to use parent_request_signature (path+user_id+first_payload_hash) for 429 cases.

root_cause: Gateway/SDK interaction where client-side retries after 429 do not preserve original X-Request-Id/idempotency header. Billing reconciliation relied primarily on request_id for deduplication; when missing, retries were treated as distinct requests resulting in duplicate token accounting.
linked_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12400 (reconciliation: add fallback signature dedupe for historical invoices)
actions_taken: Applied provisional credit of $18,400 to Acme Health on 2026-03-08 (billing ticket BL-4521).
Deployed reconciliation hotfix to apply conservative dedupe for daily aggregates and reprocessed Feb 2026 billing window to produce corrected invoice drafts.
Opened PRs to gateway and SDK teams to ensure X-Request-Id is preserved across retries after 429 responses.
Added additional logging in ingress path to capture original_request_id when present and annotation on retry events.
Notified Growth/CS with customer-friendly explanation and ETA for permanent fix and final credit reconciliation.
Scheduled postmortem writeup and cross-team review for 2026-03-15.
resolution: Hotfix to reconciliation job deployed and reprocessed affected billing window. SDK and gateway patches in review; once merged they will prevent future occurrences. Final credit amount confirmed and applied to Acme Health invoice (final credit $17,950 after minor usage cleanup).
next_steps: Merge and release gateway and SDK PRs (owners: infra-gateway, sdk-team). Target release: 2026-03-18.
Add an automated reconciliation alert that trips when daily token delta > 5% vs rolling 7-day baseline for an org.
Audit other invoice windows for similar patterns in the past 90 days and issue credits where applicable.
Update public SDK retry docs to recommend preserving idempotency/request headers and add example patterns for handling 429 throttles.
Follow-up postmortem review with CS and Billing Ops to close customer communication loop by 2026-03-16.
notes_for_reviews: Decision trade-off: prefer adding conservative dedupe in reconciliation rather than immediate gateway-only fix to limit customer impact while gateway/SDK patches progress.
Security review not required for the hotfix since only billing logic and internal logs changed (no customer secrets exposed).
